extracted.intended_audience: educators, school inspectors, education policymakers, members of learned societies (British Association) interested in primary/secondary/university education reform
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and standards for designing and evaluating primary (elementary) education and its relation to secondary and university education, emphasising practical methods, curriculum continuity, and scientific inquiry in education policy and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three pivots for instruction (Field, Workshop, Home)
rubrics_metrics.description: These three objects — the Field, the Workshop, and the Home — should be the pivots on which the scheme of instruction should be fixed, the central thoughts determining the character of the teaching to be given in rural and urban schools for boys and girls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group school studies around a practical centre furnished by outdoor pursuits, workshop exercises, and domestic arts to give unity and interest to subjects of instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach by practical methods / object-lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem of primary education is to teach by practical methods the elements of letters and of science, the art of accurate expression, the ability to think and to control the will; ordinary school lessons should lead to clear apprehension of processes that bring the child into intimate relation with the world in which he moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outdoor pursuits, manual exercises and familiar objects to excite and maintain interest in English, arithmetic, elementary science, and drawing; treat practical lessons as central rather than as mere extras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase opportunities for self-instruction; less formal teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: The child should receive less formal teaching and opportunities for self-instruction, through outdoor pursuits, manual exercises, or the free use of books, should be increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in view the rapid and marvelous stimulation of intelligence in infancy; design lessons that permit observation, experimentation and independent discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate instruction by locality and sex (country vs town; boys vs girls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise the essential difference between the requirements of country and of town life, and the training proper to boys and girls; avoid one-size-fits-all mechanical codes of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt curriculum and methods to local conditions and likely future occupations to produce relevant and diverse instruction rather than enforced uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate manual training into continuous education
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual training should form part of the child's continuous education; it should not be regarded as something apart from the school instruction with special grants and inconsistent conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate manual work with other subjects, forge a connecting link between Kindergarten teaching and workshop practice in the school, and remove conditions that treat hand-work as an external add-on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical instruction aims to train intelligence, not solely vocational skill
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim and purpose of practical instruction in primary schools, whether in cookery or other subjects, is to train the intelligence through familiar occupations, to show how scientific method may be usefully applied, and how manipulative skill may be incidentally acquired — not to train professional practitioners at that age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid narrow vocational framing (e.g., treating cookery for 12–14 year olds as training professional cooks); emphasise mental and moral training, cleanliness, order, accuracy and scientific observation in practical lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use practical science lessons to stimulate imagination and understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical lessons in chemistry and cookery provide interesting, memorable demonstrations of scientific processes (e.g., starch in rice, coagulation of egg white) that awaken children's imagination and teach scientific facts and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ demonstrative, hands-on experiments in everyday contexts to illustrate scientific principles and to quicken intelligence more effectively than abstract grammar analysis for young children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary curriculum must prepare majority for occupations and allow seamless secondary transition
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised curriculum shall provide the most suitable preparatory training for the occupations in which four-fifths of the children will subsequently be engaged, and at the same time enable them or some of them to pass without any breach of continuity from the primary to the secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design primary education that serves both immediate vocational needs and forms a sound basis for secondary/higher education; avoid producing curricula that force early, irreversible specialization or class-based separations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject class distinctions between elementary and state-aided secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no class distinctions separating the public elementary from the State-aided secondary school; schemes of primary education should be unaffected by such criticism and should serve children of all classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure curricula permit mobility and continuity so that children from elementary schools can move into secondary education without discontinuity or prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary education pervaded by the spirit of the Kindergarten
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme of primary education pervaded by the spirit of the Kindergarten which, by practical exercises, encourages observation and develops the reasoning faculties, and creates in the pupil an understanding of the use of books, would form a fitting foundation for either a literary or a scientific training in a secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise play-like, exploratory, observational activities and early development of reasoning and book-usage skills as foundational for later specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid starting instruction at the wrong end — evolve from familiar things
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of taking the child away from familiar surroundings into strange and artificial conditions, evolve teaching from the things with which the child is already familiar and in which he is likely to find his life's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base lessons on the child's everyday environment and likely life contexts to make education meaningful and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat practical teaching as essential, not an overcrowded extra
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical teaching has sometimes been treated as a sort of extra to be added to an already overcrowded literary curriculum; it should be regarded as essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restructure curricula to integrate practical lessons as core elements rather than optional add-ons that are squeezed out by literary/academic overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply scientific/inductive methods to educational problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should be considered among the sciences; knowledge of the history of education and application of methods of scientific inquiry may help to solve many intricate questions involved in establishing a national system of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test proposed reforms by scientific standards, use historical and contemporary data, and favour inductive inquiry in policy and curricular design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities' twofold function and subordinate role of examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities must be schools for preparing students for the higher duties of citizenship and professional life, and institutions for the prosecution of research; examinations for degrees, necessary as tests of acquired knowledge, must be regarded as subordinate to these two great functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate university quality by its success in research and civic/professional preparation rather than by exam outcomes alone; design assessments that support these functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local authorities should use scientific measurements and heed expert advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Local bodies possess powers under new acts to institute scientific measurements (e.g., anthropometric records), but elected local authorities sometimes distrust expert advice and act independently, which can lead to waste of effort and means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage local authorities to adopt scientific measurement practices and to rely appropriately on expert guidance to improve educational provision and public understanding.
